newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma warns Ukraine to leave port alone.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma warns Ukraine to leave port alone.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament on Thursday warned Ukraine that Moscow would never hand over control of the Crimean port of Sevastopol, home to the disputed Black Sea fleet.

The State Duma made the warning in an appeal passed just a day after deputies voted overwhelmingly to halt division between Russia and Ukraine of the 600-vessel fleet. The non-binding appeal is likely to put more pressure on already strained relations between Moscow and Kiev.

Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma is due to meet ailing Russian leader Boris Yeltsin on Thursday but the encounter looks set to be overshadowed by the latest flare-up in a five-year row over the fate of the fleet and port.

Broad accords have already been signed dividing the fleet but no decision has been reached on a share-out of bases and the future of Sevastopol, which the Duma said still fell under Russian jurisdiction although Crimea is now part of Ukraine.

"Sevastopol was, is and will be the main naval base of Russia's Black Sea fleet. Unilateral moves by Ukraine to divide it will lead not just to the division but the destruction of the Black Sea fleet -- the Duma thinks the division of the fleet has to be stopped," read the appeal.

The Duma appeal said that a Soviet decree of 1948 which put Sevastopol under Moscow's direct rule was still valid and that Russia, as the successor state to the Soviet Union, therefore still had jurisdiction over the port.
